report.clinical_summary: The patient is a lawyer diagnosed with Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) a few years ago. They present with persistent fatigue, tender swollen lymph nodes in the neck, and occasional night sweats. They've been on Ritalin for about a month (switched from Wellbutrin due to side effects) and are experiencing intense, persistent headaches that are exacerbating their anxiety. They're in a 'watch and wait' approach with stable blood cell counts but feel uneasy about not having active treatment. The patient expresses significant emotional distress, feeling the disease has 'taken over everything' including work and family time. They're worried about maintaining their career as a lawyer and fear the illness will impact their relationships and hobbies. They believe CLL is largely genetic and related to environmental factors, with family history of various cancers contributing. The patient makes efforts to stay active and eat healthily but finds it difficult due to fatigue. They want practical guidance and strategies to manage symptoms so they don't control their life completely.
